title: A 1920s adobe with Gaudí curves and a glass atrium, and I lost my mind a little
story: I helped my client Diva Zappa sell 742 North Sycamore, a 1920s Hollywood adobe a previous owner, Christopher Lloyd, had lovingly transformed and made his own. He left an actual mold of his face somewhere in that house. What most people don't realize is how much of what made this house extraordinary came from Diva herself. She's the one who brought it back to life, restoring what had been lost, rebuilding entire parts of it, and genuinely bringing the magic back into a place that could have just as easily stayed dormant. It closed at $2.82M, and Diva was an absolute dream through every twist, sewer line drama included.
pullQuote: Some houses are just square footage. This one had a piece of my childhood built into the walls.

title: A buyer's win in Glendale
story: I represented the buyer on 2621 East Glenoaks Boulevard in Glendale, which closed at an even $2,000,000. Even after we closed, I stayed on top of the details that mattered, chasing down a fire hazard disclosure issue with escrow so my buyer never had to think twice about it. That's the job as far as I'm concerned: the work doesn't stop the moment the keys change hands. Funny enough, that buyer was Diva, the same client I later helped sell her Sycamore home. I love when it works out that way.

title: Diva Zappa, Seller
story: Julia is amazing. She helped refine and curate my house before we put it on the market and honestly, the house had never been more beautiful. The entire process of buying and selling can be stressful, scary, and daunting. I don't know how she managed to make every part of the process feel so easy and empowering, but she did.
